title: Ledger and Will
premise: Edmund Ashgrove, an insurance investigator whose photographic memory has made them both invaluable and isolated, receives two letters about the same drowned man: one confessing to his murder, the other promising that more deaths will follow unless a decade-old verdict stands undisturbed. Pulled back to the coastal town of Marrow Bay, where they once testified in the case everyone swore was closed, Edmund must reconstruct what really happened the night Tobias Wren went into the sea—using only their memory of documents, faces, and lies. As the promised deaths begin and the tide erodes the shoreline where the truth is buried, Edmund realizes the letters were written by someone who knows them intimately: the person they helped make invisible years ago. In the end, Edmund must choose between preserving their own anonymity and exposing a conspiracy that includes the mentor who taught them to disappear.
about_author: Jude Amberdale is the pen name of a former maritime claims adjuster who spent eleven years investigating deaths at sea before turning to fiction. They write from a house on an eroding cliff, which they insist is not a metaphor.

chapters.title: Two Envelopes, One Hand
chapters.summary: Edmund Ashgrove's POV. A quiet archivist of other people's tragedies, Edmund receives twin letters about Tobias Wren—a drowning ruled accidental ten years ago, a case Edmund helped close. One letter confesses; the other promises more. The handwriting on both is identical, and Edmund recognizes it, though they can't place from where. Emotional beat: dread dressed as curiosity.

chapters.title: The Verdict Everyone Signed
chapters.summary: Edmund travels to Marrow Bay, revisiting the case file from memory—every signature, every inconsistency they once chose not to flag. Flashbacks reveal young Edmund testifying, eager to please, omitting a detail that would have unraveled everything. Emotional beat: guilt surfacing like something the tide returns.

chapters.title: What the Widow Keeps Locked
chapters.summary: Edmund interviews Marion Wren, the widow, who is neither grieving nor surprised by Edmund's return. She reveals Tobias had been auditing the town's largest employer, Harrow Point Cannery, and that his ledger disappeared with him. Third-person limited shifts briefly to Marion. Emotional beat: the unease of being expected.

chapters.title: A Death on Schedule
chapters.summary: The second promised death arrives precisely as foretold: the cannery's former foreman drowns in his bathtub, dry land be damned. Edmund's photographic recall spots a forged time-stamp in the coroner's report—the same forgery technique used ten years ago. Emotional beat: horror sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: The Mentor's Kindness
chapters.summary: Edmund seeks out Aldous Vane, the retired investigator who trained them, now a respected town fixture. Vane warns them off gently, then not so gently, revealing he knows about the detail Edmund omitted a decade ago. Flashback deepens: Vane taught Edmund that invisibility is safety. Emotional beat: betrayal beginning its slow bloom.

chapters.title: Ledger Pages in a Gull's Nest
chapters.summary: Following the confession letter's riddling clues, Edmund finds torn ledger pages hidden in the cliffs—evidence the cannery was laundering money through falsified death claims, claims Edmund themselves processed without ever looking closely. Their own name appears in the margins. Emotional beat: complicity made physical.

chapters.title: The Third Letter Arrives Early
chapters.summary: The pattern breaks: a third letter arrives ahead of schedule, addressed not to Edmund but to Marion, forcing Edmund to protect the one witness who trusts them. A near-fatal encounter on the tidal flats leaves Edmund certain the letter-writer is watching them in real time. Emotional beat: paranoia becoming intimacy—they know this watcher.

chapters.title: Everyone Who Swore
chapters.summary: Edmund confronts the closed circle: Vane, the coroner, the harbormaster—all swore the case shut, all profited from keeping it shut. Under pressure, the coroner confesses to falsifying the autopsy but insists Tobias was already dead when he saw him, killed by someone above them all. Emotional beat: the conspiracy's architecture exposed, its keystone still hidden.

chapters.title: What the Tide Gives Up
chapters.summary: Climax. At low tide, the eroding shore yields Tobias's remains—and with them, proof he didn't drown but was struck before entering the water. Edmund lures the killer to the flats using the promise-letter's own language: it was Vane, who murdered Tobias to protect the laundering scheme and has been grooming, testing, and tormenting Edmund ever since, proud of the instrument he made. Emotional beat: recognition, rage, and the terrible relief of certainty.

chapters.title: A Name in the Margin
chapters.summary: Resolution. Vane arrested, the town's ledger opened, Edmund testifies again—this time withholding nothing, including their own omission. Marion offers them a place in Marrow Bay, and for the first time Edmund considers belonging rather than invisibility. The final image: Edmund burning the confession letter, keeping only the promise, now fulfilled differently. Emotional beat: identity chosen, not hidden.
